reasoning: Every load-bearing fact holds and the arithmetic is exact at the correct 15.625 Hz timebase. DRADAR is JSRed exactly once (grep: sole JSR at BZONE.MAC:510) inside the once-per-frame display-list build (routine starts BZONE.MAC:425 with the BUFRDY buffer-wait and INC FRAME at :439); line :1085 labels the boundary 'END OF FRAME (64 MS)'. So the +0x0B increment is per game frame (15.625 Hz), not per $INTCT. SANGLE is a single byte (.BLKB 1 at :250) and is written ONLY at :3898 (grep confirms one STA SANGLE), inside DRADAR, so no override. The increment operand 0B is in the .RADIX 16 region (.RADIX 16 at :3, flips to .RADIX 10 only at :4878) with no trailing period, so 0x0B = 11 decimal. The 256-unit byte-angle circle is independently proven by TRACK:3525 'LDA I,20 ;C USE 45 DEG' — 0x20=32, 32/256*360 = 45 deg exactly. Arithmetic: 256/11 = 23.2727 frames/rev; x64ms = 1489.45 ms/rev = 0.6714 rev/s = 15.469 deg/frame. Ours SWEEP_PERIOD_MS=2000 (radar.ts:58) = 0.5 rev/s = 11.52 deg/frame at 64ms; 2000/1489.45 = 1.343, i.e. ~34% too slow. False-60Hz check: 23.27x16.667 = 388 ms, so 2000 matches neither 1489 nor 388 — it is an unsourced round number. Our sweepAngle() (radar.ts:98) advances in real ms decoupled from frame count. All numbers match the finding to the digit; no correction needed.

The blip is a decaying byte-timer, not a boolean, and our core carries no equivalent. BLIP is defined as 'BLIMP TIMER' (BZONE.MAC:298) and is written only at :3948 (set) and :4059 (decay) per grep. On a sweep pass it is armed to 0xF0=240 (:3947-3948); DR.BLP subtracts hex 8 each frame (SBC I,8 at :4058, STA BLIP at :4059) whenever nonzero — I traced that DR.BLP is reached once per DRADAR call (once per 64ms frame). 0xF0/8 = 30 frames = 30x64 = 1920 ms ~= 1.92 s fade, all radix-16 operands. Because the fade (1920 ms) exceeds the sweep period (1489 ms from D-001), an in-range target is re-armed to 240 while BLIP has only decayed to 240 - 23.27x8 = ~54, so it never blinks fully off and pulses per pass — verified. Ours: RadarBlip carries only {bearing, range} (radar.ts:39-48), deriveRadar unconditionally pushes each blip (radar.ts:88), and the shell renderer draws every blip as a fixed-size filled dot (render.ts:201-206) with no alpha/brightness — so nothing exists to fade. No override redeems it. Accurate.

The sweep-gate mechanism is real and precisely described. At BZONE.MAC:3941-3948 the code does LDA SANGLE / SEC / SBC GARBAG (relative bearing formed at :3935-3940), then BMI 23$ (skip if the 8-bit difference is negative) and CMP I,0C / BCS 23$ (skip if >= 0x0C=12), re-lighting BLIP<-0xF0 only when (SANGLE - relative bearing) is in [0, 0x0C). 0C is radix-16 (region governs to :4878); 12/256*360 = 16.875 deg trailing window — exact. So the blip is re-armed only as the rotating arm crosses the target bearing, then decays (D-002). Ours has no such gate: deriveRadar (radar.ts:75) never references the sweep and pushes every visible contact unconditionally (radar.ts:88); sweepAngle (radar.ts:98) is passed to the shell (main.ts:234) and used only to STROKE the sweep line (render.ts:195-198), never to gate blip output (render.ts:201-206 draw all blips every frame). The finding's precise wording 'never consumed to gate blip output' is accurate; the looser 'computed but never consumed' is a minor imprecision (it is consumed to draw the line) that does not touch the substance. Mechanism divergence is genuine.

Accurate and appropriately scoped as a benign model-generality divergence (class DIVERGENCE, recommendation accept). DRADAR calls TRACK exactly once (BZONE.MAC:3934) and TRACK computes the relative position of a SINGLE object ('HIS XPOS MINUS ROBOT XPOS', :3488-3509) with no loop over an enemy list; the whole routine draws at most one VGDOT blip (:4038). The R2D3FL flag selects tank OR missile as the one tracked hostile, so even with both present the ROM paints one blip. Ours: deriveRadar loops over all contacts (radar.ts:80) and pushes one blip per radar-visible contact, unbounded — a real property of the core API. In practice it is harmless: radarContacts (enemies.ts:727) returns at most ONE hostile (the single state.hostile if alive) and the saucer is filtered, so our live game already draws at most one blip, exactly as the finding hedges ('not a live defect'). The finding correctly states the ROM fact, our API generality, and the benign scope; it survives as an accurate observation.

The max-range gate exists in the ROM and is absent in ours. At BZONE.MAC:3975-3978, A holds TDIST (the distance high byte MOUTHI, :3961-3963); CMP I,80 / BCC 35$ takes the in-range blip-draw path (35$, the only path reaching VGDOT at :4038) only when TDIST < 0x80. When TDIST >= 0x80 (carry set, no branch) it falls to :3979-3980 LDA I,0 / STA EIRNGE (clears the 'ENEMY IN RANGE FLAG', defined :258) and routes via TANKCK/R2D3CK to JMP DR.BLP (:3987-3989), which only decays BLIP and never draws a dot — so an out-of-range target paints no blip that frame. 0x80 is radix-16. Ours has no cutoff: deriveRadar computes range=hypot(dx,dz) (radar.ts:87) and emits every contact unconditionally; the shell only CLAMPS range to the scope edge (Math.min(b.range/RADAR_RANGE,1)*R, render.ts:202) and still fills the dot, so a target at any distance still paints. The finding is honest that the world-unit value of 0x80 is not derivable from DRADAR alone (it is the TRACK matrix-mult magnitude high byte) and scopes the fix to 'add a max-range gate, threshold TBD from TRACK'. Accurate.
